version.changelog:
- Enterprise onboarding instructions added, allowing managed device enrollment with private Core deployments.
- New uninstall process: uses a script for complete cleanup, removing config, plugin files, and credentials.
- Documentation refinements, including clearer separation for "human" and agent protection and expanded plan details.
- Version updated from 6.7.23 to 6.8.14.

llm.summary: The SKILL.md is coherent with a security plugin install flow, but it instructs installing and running external plugin code that will persist on disk and handle API keys — risks that should be reviewed before proceeding.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (runtime security guard) align with the instructions: installing a MoltGuard plugin, checking status, performing tests, and enrolling agents. There are no unrelated requirements (no unrelated env vars or binaries requested).
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The instructions tell the agent/user to install an external plugin and then read and execute files under ~/.openclaw/extensions/moltguard/ and save credentials to ~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard/. In particular, they instruct running node scripts (enterprise-enroll.mjs / enterprise-unenroll.mjs / uninstall.mjs) which will execute code from the installed plugin. Those steps go beyond mere documentation and implicitly require executing remote code and handling secrets.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill has no embedded install spec but directs the user to run 'openclaw plugins install @openguardrails/moltguard', which will fetch and install third-party code. Because the skill bundle contains no code to audit, you must trust the package source and its contents before installing. This is a moderate-to-high risk action in practice (remote code download/execute).
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill itself does not request env vars or credentials, but the workflow expects an API key from 'Core' and describes saving credentials to a local path and sharing an account/quota across agents. Centralizing API keys and linking multiple agents to one account is functionally consistent but increases exposure if the plugin or Core endpoint is compromised.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (normal). However, installing the plugin will persist files and credentials under the user's home and may run scripts on restart. Persistent presence combined with external code install and stored API keys increases the blast radius if the plugin is malicious or vulnerable.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This SKILL.md is a usage/install guide for an external OpenClaw plugin rather than packaged code you can audit in-line. Before installing: (1) verify the package origin (@openguardrails/moltguard) and inspect its repository and published package contents (look for the node scripts it references); (2) confirm the plugin's release source (npm/GitHub releases) and review recent commits/issues; (3) be cautious about sharing or centralizing API keys — prefer per-agent keys or scoped credentials; (4) run the install in a safe/sandboxed environment first, and review any scripts under ~/.openclaw/extensions/moltguard/ before executing them; (5) if you need enterprise enrollment, validate the target Core URL and TLS authenticity to avoid sending data to an attacker-controlled endpoint. Because the skill delegates installation to external code that will persist and manage credentials, treat it as untrusted until you've audited the plugin.
